questions.q: What should the Executive Summary page be designed to do?
options: Answer the Sales Director's headline questions in seconds, not invite exploration
Show every column from every table in the model
Replace the Drill-Down page entirely
Require the Sales Director to write their own DAX
questions.explain: This page is built for a time-constrained audience who needs a glance, not a deep exploration tool.

questions.q: Which visuals does this lesson add to the Executive Summary page?
options: KPI cards (Total Sales, Average Order Value, Total Units), a weekly trend line, a Region slicer, and a Pct of Company Total card
A single table listing every order line
A map visual only
A matrix broken out by every product subcategory
questions.explain: The page is built around headline KPIs, a trend chart, and light regional context, per the Sales Director's requirements from Lesson 1.

questions.q: Why does the model's Fields pane create a real hazard when building this page?
options: Total Sales and Total Sales (All Regions) sit right next to each other alphabetically, and fast repetitive dragging makes a wrong pick easy to miss
Power BI limits the Fields pane to five items
The Fields pane cannot display measures, only columns
There is no hazard; every measure name is completely unique
questions.explain: Two similarly-named measures sitting adjacent in a long, alphabetized list is exactly the condition that makes a mis-drag easy during fast, repetitive card-building.

questions.q: Why might a KPI card bound to the wrong measure still look correct when you first glance at the page?
options: If the Region slicer is left on its default unselected state, Total Sales and Total Sales (All Regions) return the same number
Power BI always displays the correct number regardless of binding
Wrong measures are automatically flagged with a red icon
It can never look correct; a wrong binding is always visibly obvious
questions.explain: With no region filter applied, ALL(TerritoryDim) has nothing to strip away, so the two measures coincidentally match until a filter is actually applied.

questions.q: What does the Lab for this lesson ask you to check, specifically leaving the Region slicer unselected?
options: That all four cards show a number in the slicer's default state
That the page fails to load without a region selected
That the trend line chart is empty by default
That Average Order Value always shows zero
questions.explain: The lab mirrors how you'd naturally review a freshly built page — before applying any filter.
